steps.action: Call your bank, or the bank the money went to, right now. Say it was a phone scam and ask them to freeze the account (지급정지). Police 112 or the FSS 1332 can also put you through.
Report the scam at your police station (cyber investigation unit) and ask for the incident report certificate (사건사고사실확인원).
Within 3 business days, take the refund request form (피해구제신청서), a copy of your ID and the police certificate to the bank branch where you asked for the freeze.
steps.organisation: the bank that froze the account
steps.contact: the bank branch where you asked for the freeze

steps.action: Wait for a letter. The FSS posts a notice; if no one objects for 2 months, it decides your refund within 14 days and your bank pays you.

extra.lawName: 전기통신금융사기 피해 방지 및 피해자산 환급에 관한 특별법 (통신사기피해환급법)
extra.notes: Step 3 deadlineDays 3 means 3 business days (영업일). If the papers are late, the bank may give a further 14 days, after which the request counts as never made. The act was renamed from '...피해금 환급...' to '...피해자산 환급...' by Act No. 21503 (2026-03-31, in force 6 months after promulgation); it now covers crypto-asset transfers. Version in force: Act No. 22047, effective 2026-10-02. Cash handed over in person or withdrawn (대면편취형, Art. 2(2)(c)-(d)) is frozen on a police request (Art. 3(2), added 2023-05-16), not on the victim's own application. 간편송금: prepaid e-money issuers registered with the FSC must share fraud-account data with banks (Art. 15(3), added 2024-02-27; Decree Art. 11-3). Other victims of the same account can still apply within 2 months of the FSS notice (Art. 6(1)). FSS also lists freezing your own accounts at payinfo.or.kr; the police scam centre number 1394 is on counterscam112.go.kr (not an allow-listed domain, so not used as a step source). The FSS refund page still prints the old law name.

extra.lawName: 여신전문금융업법 (Credit Specialized Financial Business Act), Art. 16
extra.notes: PROPOSED: no statutory chargeback window for a card payment the victim made to a scammer was found on any allowed page; Art. 16 sets none, and card-scheme chargeback deadlines live in card-company terms. The 60-day period in Decree Art. 6-9 covers misuse of a lost or stolen card before it was reported, not a payment the victim made. Art. 16(5)2 makes the card company liable for use of card details obtained by hacking or other dishonest means. The telecom-fraud refund act excludes acts disguised as supplying goods or services, so a shopping-scam card payment is not on that path.
